2026_005_m051926bdmtg.paragraph: Regular meeting minutes of the Troy Board of Education for Tuesday, May 19, 2026, at the Service Center, 4420 Livernois, Troy, MI 48098, filed in the June 16, 2026 board packet. President Anne called the meeting to order at 7:00 p.m. with all seven members present and roughly 125 people in the audience; recognitions honored Outstanding Support Person of the Year Matt Snitgen, Legislative CAP students, Schools of Character honorees and volunteers. The most consequential action was award of the Boulan Park Middle School renovation bid at $297,803.00 from the Capital Projects Fund, alongside a $205,610.00 vehicle purchase from Gorno Ford.
2026_005_m051926bdmtg.page:
**Meeting**
Troy Board of Education regular meeting, Tuesday, May 19, 2026, at the Troy School District Services Building, 4420 Livernois, Troy, MI 48098. Called to order by President Anne at 7:00 p.m.; adjourned at 8:27 p.m. Filed under the June 16, 2026 packet.

**Attendance**
Board members Anne, Alic, Haupt, Melton, Philippart, Potts and Zendler. Also present: Superintendent Machesky and administrators DiPilato, Griffor, Keegan, Cottone, Wallace, Cronin, Griffin, Hall, Montante, Pagel and Trudel, plus approximately 125 members of the audience.

**Recognitions**
- Outstanding Support Person of the Year: Matt Snitgen, a paraprofessional in the MOCI Room at Athens High School, nominated by Rebecca Roy from a field of 25 nominees.
- Legislative Career Accelerator Program: teachers Brynn Lawrence (Troy Center for Transition) and Mark Chrzanowski (International Academy East) introduced Ava Pittman and Nathan Kohnert; participating students were Ayush Jaganath, Aarshia Soni, Harini Shrii Vengata Raghavan (Troy High), Tasnia Jannah, Sulayma Setiaarif (Athens), Amal Surti and Syeda Tarannum (IAE).
- Schools of Character: Hamilton Elementary and Troy Union Elementary named National Schools of Character by Character.org, two of just 72 schools nationwide; Schroeder Elementary, Troy Union and Boulan Park Middle School named State Schools of Character; Wattles and Barnard Elementary received Honorable Mention; Troy Union and Wattles were the only Michigan schools recognized for Promising Practices.
- Volunteers: Athens - Kristin Kennaugh, Heather and Kevin Blum, Samantha Zoll; IAE - Harj Deol, Minal Kulkarni, Surya Saladi; Troy High - Cheri Armstrong, Sherry Gillespie.

**Actions and votes**

| Item | Moved / supported | Vote |
| --- | --- | --- |
| National Teacher Appreciation Week, May 4-8, 2026 | Zendler / Potts | Yes 7, No 0 |
| Mental Health Awareness Month, May 2026 | Potts / Philippart | Yes 7, No 0 |
| Consent agenda items A through L | Haupt / Alic | Yes 7, No 0 |
| Boulan Park renovation bid, $297,803.00 | Philippart / Zendler | Yes 7, No 0 |
| Food Service and Operations vehicles, $205,610.00 | Alic / Haupt | Yes 7, No 0 |
| Oakland Schools biennial election resolution | Philippart / Haupt | Yes 7, No 0 |

The mental health resolution cited Oakland Community Health Network, stated that one in five Americans experience mental health issues, and referenced National Children's Mental Health Awareness Day on May 7, 2026 and Children's Mental Health Acceptance Week, May 3 through May 9, 2026.

**Consent agenda (A through L)**
Minutes of the April 7, 2026 special meeting and workshop, the April 14, 2026 special meeting, the April 21, 2026 regular meeting, and the April 28, 2026 special meeting, closed session and workshop; the Treasurer's Report for March 2026; approval of the Oakland Intermediate School District budget; a resolution to hold a public hearing on the proposed 2026/2027 school year budget; IA budget approval for 2026/2027; and a K-8 literacy pilot purchase. Personnel and Curriculum had no items.

**Business**
The bid for a complete renovation of Boulan Park Middle School covering architectural, mechanical, electrical and structural work (recommendation 3 of 3) was awarded at $297,803.00 as an expenditure of the Capital Projects Fund. The bid for a Food Services vehicle and an Operations vehicle was awarded to Gorno Ford at $205,610.00, charged to the Food Services Fund and the Maintenance Improvement Fund.

**Oakland Schools biennial election**
Under Mich. Comp. Laws 380.614, the board designated Kendra Montante as its representative, with a member of the district administration team as alternate, to the 2026 electoral body electing the Oakland Schools Intermediate School District Board of Education; supported candidate Gary Hauff for the one position, a six-year term ending June 30, 2032; and directed Montante to vote for Hauff at least on the first ballot at the June 1, 2026 election.

**Reports and comments**
Student representatives Chloe Gentilini (Troy College and Career High School), Ahyoung Song (International Academy-East), Sara Graunstadt (Athens High School) and Bella Doss (Troy High School) reported. One community member spoke during non-agenda public communication; no action was taken. Board comments covered the Oakland County enhancement millage, budget reductions against a $12 million deficit, the TFEE Golf Outing on June 9, retiree recognition June 1 at Troy High, and Coffee with the Superintendent and Board on May 21 at 5:00 pm. The next workshop was set for Tuesday, June 1 at Troy High and the next regular meeting for Tuesday, June 16 at the Services Building. Submitted by Matt Haupt, Secretary.
2026_005_m051926bdmtg.verbose:
**Identification**
Regular meeting minutes of the Troy Board of Education, Tuesday, May 19, 2026, held at the Troy School District Services Building (Service Center), 4420 Livernois, Troy, MI 48098. The record is filed as M051926BdMtg within the June 16, 2026 board packet. President Anne called the meeting to order at 7:00 p.m. and it was adjourned at 8:27 p.m. Minutes were respectfully submitted by Matt Haupt, Secretary of the Troy Board of Education, with typist initials MH/jh.

**Attendance**
In addition to Mrs. Anne, board members Alic, Haupt, Melton, Philippart, Potts and Zendler were present. Also present were Superintendent Machesky and administrators DiPilato, Griffor, Keegan, Cottone, Wallace, Cronin, Griffin, Hall, Montante, Pagel and Trudel. Approximately 125 members of the audience attended. The meeting opened with the Pledge of Allegiance.

**Recognition: Outstanding Support Staff**
The board presented the Outstanding Support Person of the Year award, a category covering bus drivers, secretaries, paraprofessionals, student support aides, custodial staff, food service, technology, childcare, security and more. There were 25 nominees. The 2026 honoree is Matt Snitgen, a paraprofessional at Athens High School in the MOCI Room, nominated by Rebecca Roy. The nomination praised his unwavering belief in his students, noting that he sees potential where others often see limitations, and cited his positivity, compassion and work ethic. It described how he models and encourages communication in all forms, including body language, gestures, facial expressions and AAC devices, treating every communicative attempt as meaningful. A student was quoted saying, "We have a secret handshake. Mr. S is a great person because he's nice and he makes me feel happy and excited to be at school." Snitgen's name was engraved on the Support Person Plaque, to be displayed at his building for the next year, and a short video of the surprise visit was shown.

**Legislative CAP Students Report**
Students from the Legislative track of the Career Accelerator Program (CAP) reported on their engagement with the school board, the city, and state senators and representatives. Troy Center for Transition teacher Brynn Lawrence and International Academy East teacher Mark Chrzanowski were invited to the podium to introduce their students. Ava Pittman of IA-East and Nathan Kohnert of TCT described their experience and shared a brief video. CAP students who shared their experiences were Ayush Jaganath (Troy High), Tasnia Jannah (Athens), Sulayma Setiaarif (Athens), Aarshia Soni (Troy High), Amal Surti (IAE), Syeda Tarannum (IAE) and Harini Shrii Vengata Raghavan (Troy High).

**Schools of Character Recognition**
Hamilton Elementary School and Troy Union Elementary School were honored as National Schools of Character, two of just 72 schools nationwide to receive the distinction from Character.org. The designation recognizes schools that use character development to positively impact academics, student behavior and school culture. Schroeder Elementary School, Troy Union Elementary School and Boulan Park Middle School were named State Schools of Character, and Wattles Elementary School and Barnard Elementary School received Honorable Mention. Character.org also recognized Troy Union and Wattles as the only schools in Michigan to earn recognition for Promising Practices, highlighting innovative efforts that strengthen school culture, encourage student leadership and service, and promote goodness in action.

**Volunteer Appreciation**
April is Volunteer Appreciation Month, and the board thanked volunteers whose students graduate from TSD this year. Parents recognized and given a token of appreciation were: Athens - Kristin Kennaugh, Heather and Kevin Blum, and Samantha Zoll; IAE - Harj Deol, Minal Kulkarni, and Surya Saladi; Troy High - Cheri Armstrong and Sherry Gillespie.

**National Teacher Appreciation Week resolution**
Teacher Appreciation Week was celebrated Monday, May 4 through Friday, May 8, 2026. Moved by Mrs. Zendler and supported by Mrs. Potts, the resolution recited that teachers inspire and open children's minds, promote and strengthen the principles of democratic equality, develop leaders and encourage critical thinking, and that Troy teachers set the bar for excellence. It resolved that the Troy School District supports National Teacher Appreciation Week, May 4-8, 2026. Vote: Yes 7, No 0.

**Mental Health Awareness Month resolution**
Introduced with reference to Oakland Community Health Network and its service provider network and to other school boards across Oakland County. Moved by Mrs. Potts and supported by Dr. Philippart, the resolution recited that one in five of all Americans, including children, experience mental health issues that could lead to school difficulties, physical problems and even suicide; that May 7, 2026 is designated National Children's Mental Health Awareness Day; and that May 3 through May 9, 2026 is designated Children's Mental Health Acceptance Week. It resolved that the Troy Board of Education recognizes May 2026 as Mental Health Awareness Month. Vote: Yes 7, No 0.

**Procedural**
A five-minute recess followed the recognitions. There were no additions or deletions to the agenda and no public communication on agenda items.

**Consent agenda**
Moved by Mr. Haupt and supported by Mrs. Alic, the board approved items A through L: minutes of the April 7, 2026 Special Board of Education Meeting; minutes of the April 7, 2026 Board of Education Workshop; minutes of the April 14, 2026 Special Board of Education Meeting; minutes of the April 21, 2026 Board of Education Meeting; minutes of the April 28, 2026 Special Board of Education Meeting; minutes of the April 28, 2026 Closed Session Meeting; minutes of the April 28, 2026 Board of Education Workshop; the Treasurer's Report for March 2026; Approve Oakland Intermediate School District Budget; a Resolution to Hold a Public Hearing on the Proposed 2026/2027 School Year Budget; IA Budget Approval for the 2026/2027 School Year; and the K-8 Literacy Pilot Purchase. Vote: Yes 7, No 0. The Personnel and Curriculum sections contained no items.

**Business: Boulan Park Renovation Project (Recommendation 3 of 3)**
Moved by Dr. Philippart and supported by Mrs. Zendler, the board resolved that the bid for a complete renovation of Boulan Park Middle School, including architectural, mechanical, electrical and structural work, be awarded as attached in the amount of $297,803.00, and that the amount be approved as an expenditure of the Capital Projects Fund. Vote: Yes 7, No 0.

**Business: Purchase of Replacement Vehicles for Food Service and Operations**
Moved by Mrs. Alic and supported by Mr. Haupt, the board resolved that the bid for a Food Services vehicle and an Operations vehicle be awarded to Gorno Ford in the amount of $205,610.00, approved as an expenditure of the Food Services Fund and the Maintenance Improvement Fund. Vote: Yes 7, No 0.

**Public communication (non-agenda items)**
One community member addressed the board. No action was taken by the board.

**Other: Oakland Schools Biennial Election**
Moved by Dr. Philippart and supported by Mr. Haupt. The resolution recited that Mich. Comp. Laws section 380.614 requires a constituent school board to designate its representative and identify the Intermediate School Board candidate it supports by a resolution adopted not earlier than 21 days prior to the election; that the statute prescribes consideration of the resolution at not less than one public meeting before adoption; and that the board previously considered the resolution at an open meeting conducted under the Open Meetings Act on May 19, 2026. The board designated Kendra Montante as its representative and a member of the Troy School District administration team as its alternate representative to serve on the 2026 electoral body responsible for electing members to the Oakland Schools Intermediate School District Board of Education. The board supported candidate Gary Hauff for the one position on that board for a term of six years ending June 30, 2032, and directed representative Kendra Montante to vote for Gary Hauff at least on the first ballot taken at the June 1, 2026 election. Vote: Yes 7, No 0.

**Reports from high school student representatives**
Chloe Gentilini reported for Troy College and Career High School; Ahyoung Song for International Academy-East; Sara Graunstadt for Athens High School; and Bella Doss for Troy High School, each on events and activities at their schools.

**Board comments**
Topics raised included Troy Youth Assistance Recognition; the Troy Community Coalition Incredible Kid; a Troy Interfaith Group event and a Faith and Community Leaders breakfast; the TFEE Golf Outing on June 9; the Larson Celebration of Learning event; Operation Belonging at Athens; retirees recognition June 1 at Troy High; Teacher Appreciation Week; thanks to volunteers; an Oakland County Government Relations Committee legislative update by Mrs. Alic; the Oakland County Enhancement Millage; budget reductions in connection with a $12 million deficit; a salmon release at Riverbends Park; TSD and Robotics partnering to find a site for teams to work; the SSAB Middle School Leadership Conference; Mental Health Awareness and the Red Pillar; congratulations to graduating senior board representatives; Coffee with the Superintendent and Board on May 21 at 5:00 pm; and congratulations to the 2026 graduates.

**Upcoming meetings and adjournment**
The next board workshop was scheduled for Tuesday, June 1 at Troy High, and the next regular meeting for Tuesday, June 16 at the Services Building. The meeting was adjourned at 8:27 p.m.

Each sheet prices a configuration option by option against Hoekstra, Holland and Midwest Transit, marking items as standard equipment, no charge or not available, and closes with product base price, configured price, unit price, total price and grand total. Hoekstra carries the lowest grand total on most specs; Holland comes in lower on the 77-passenger conventional spec #26078 at $304,976.00 and on the 77-passenger special-needs spec #26079 at $170,267.00.
